messages:
Marie Chen: Quick heads-up — hit a regression in the eval harness when bringing up llama-3-8b-q4 on dedicated nodes. Runner crashes after ~700 requests during the concurrency sweep, stacktrace below. :bug: 

Marie Chen: ```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "eval_runner/runner.py", line 214, in _process_batch
    kv_cache.update(resp.kv)
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'update'
```

Sachin Patel: I can repro on my laptop with --concurrency 16, seq_len 512. Looks like the model returns empty kv for some warmup requests and the runner doesn't guard for that. Will add a quick fix.

Eva López: Noted. This surfaced in the perf/load eval where p95 suddenly jumped from 120ms to 450ms after concurrency > 12. The crash happens shortly after. We should treat empty kv as a valid no-op, not a hard failure.

Alex Kim: Filing a tiny patch suggestion: wrap with `if resp.kv:` before updating. Also add logging `kv_missing=true` with sample request id so we can trace.

Sachin Patel: Yep. Patch prepared: ```diff
-    kv_cache.update(resp.kv)
+    if resp.kv:
+        kv_cache.update(resp.kv)
+    else:
+        logger.debug("kv_missing=true req=%s model=%s", req.id, model.name)
```
Pushing in a sec.

Anya (eng-ml): Excellent. Can we also add a metric definition to capture these kv-miss events in the harness output? I want the dashboards to show rate(kv_missing) per 1k requests.

Marie Chen: Yes — metric name proposal: `eval.kv_cache.missed_count` with tags {model, config, concurrency}. Add it to the runner emmitter and to the prometheus exporter.

Eva López: While we're changing metrics, let's clarify latency SLOs in the test config. For the perf-eval job we use: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 200ms, p99 < 400ms for seq_len <= 256. For seq_len 512 p95 < 300ms. We should encode that as assertions in CI.

Alex Kim: I noticed our current runner uses overall mean latency for the CI gate. That hides tails. Suggest replacing CI assertion with explicit p95/p99 checks and fail only when p95 exceeds threshold or kv_missing rate > 0.5% over the run.

CI Bot: New job queued: `eval-perf/llama-3-8b-q4/concurrency-sweep` (PR #4823). See https://ci.redwood.ai/job/4823. (reaction :eyes:)

Sachin Patel: CI yaml snippet I'm adding to the PR for the gate: ```yaml
jobs:
  - name: perf-eval-llama3-concurrency
    runs-on: self-hosted
    steps:
      - run: python -m eval_runner --model llama-3-8b-q4 --concurrency-sweep --seq-lens 128,256,512 --requests 2000
      - run: python tools/check_metrics.py --input results.json --assert p95<300 --assert kv_missing_rate<0.005
```

Marie Chen: Perfect. Also add a short timeout to the harness run (e.g., 30m) and archive `results.json` on failure for debugging.

Eva López: For reporting/dashboarding: create a Grafana panel in the Eval workspace with these series: latency_p50,p95,p99, throughput(req/s), kv_missing_rate, cost_per_token (USD). Link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ev-eval/perf-evals (placeholder). Panel should show concurrent runs overlayed by concurrency level. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

Alex Kim: About cost_per_token — we need the harness to emit token_count and total_gpu_ms so cost_per_token = (gpu_ms * $/gpu_hour) / (token_count) with a per-job label for chosen instance type. I'll add `job.metadata.instance_type`.

Anya (eng-ml): Also include model quantization metadata: quant_type=q4_0,q4_1,q8 etc. We need to compare quality vs cost in the same dashboard. Add `eval.quality.rouge` and `eval.quality.perplexity` where applicable.

Sachin Patel: Re: runner bug — patch merged to branch `fix/kv-guard` and running the concurrency sweep locally. Preliminary: no crash, but observed throughput drop after concurrency 24. Suspect batching knob interacts poorly with q4 kernels under high concurrency.

Marie Chen: Can you capture `batch_size_distribution` from the runtime and emit as histogram? That will help diagnose if tail requests aren't batching and causing kernel inefficiencies.

Sachin Patel: Added histogram `runtime.batch_size.dist` to the emitter. Also logged kernel fallback events.

Eva López: Running end-to-end sweep now on a dedicated pool, results: p95 at concurrency 8=140ms, concurrency 16=170ms, concurrency 24=290ms, concurrency 32=680ms (post-crash previously). Throughput flatlines ~320 req/s after 16. Cost per token rises sharply at >24 concurrency. I'll attach summary in PR comments.

Alex Kim: If throughput flatlines, maybe the model's memory copy or locking is becoming a bottleneck. Let's capture GPU utilization, PCIe bandwidth, and NVLink metrics during runs. Add `gpu.util`, `gpu.mem.used`, `gpu.memory_copy_ms` to exporter.

Anya (eng-ml): For the CI-level mock tests (fast feedback), create a reduced `smoke` config: 200 requests, concurrency 4, seq_len 128 — assert p95 < 200ms and kv_missing_rate 0. Then the full concurrency sweep lives in nightly.

Marie Chen: Agree. Action items:
- Sachin: monitor patch & collect GPU metrics (due EOD)
- Eva: upload full sweep CSV + dashboard panels (due tomorrow)
- Alex: update cost calc + job metadata (due EOD)
- Anya: add p95/p99 CI assertions and smoke job (due tomorrow)

Sachin Patel: On it. Pushing logs to `s3://redwood-eval-logs/1719004321/` after run.

CI Bot: PR #4823 status: checks pending -> running `perf-eval-llama3-concurrency`. (reaction :rocket:)

Marie Chen: Thanks team. If we stabilize kv_miss and tail p99, we should be able to onboard q4 variant for production A/B. Keep notes in the PR and add a short entry to the eval-runner changelog.

Eva López: Leaving a note for future: metric names should use kebab or dot? We're standardizing on dots (e.g., `eval.kv_cache.missed_count`) so downstream dashboards don't break.

Alex Kim: LGTM. Will iterate on dashboards after artifacts are uploaded.

Anya (eng-ml): Thanks — will close the loop once nightly sweep completes. :white_check_mark:
